scope: R189: FA roofline arithmetic - the 10 s target is 36% of GEMM efficiency, not 71%

own_error_corrected.first_attempt: omitted the head factor H=7 and concluded 3.3 TFLOPS per tile with 29x headroom
own_error_corrected.implausible_signal: 3.4% of GEMM peak is not credible for a production kernel, which is what exposed the error
own_error_corrected.corrected: per-tile flops 139.5 MFLOP after multiplying by H

tiles.tail_note: 24858 tiles over 30 cores is 828.6 waves, so tail waste is negligible

key_correction.old_framing: FA must go from 41.1 to 69 TFLOPS per card against a 96.9 GEMM peak, which reads as 71% of GEMM and sounds very hard
key_correction.both_are_dense_normalised: however 41.1 and 69 are dense figures, while a causal kernel only performs 50.5% of the tiles
key_correction.conclusion: 36% of GEMM peak is an ordinary level for a mature flash-attention kernel, so the target is materially easier than previously described

implications: FA is worth pursuing: 1.50x is needed, not the 1.68x the dense framing implied and far from matching GEMM
R171s 4.38 s upper bound assumed matching GEMM, which is not required; 2.98 s suffices for 10 s
the current 24% means each 6.00 us tile carries substantial non-cube cost that has to fall to 3.60 us
not_measured: this is arithmetic, not measurement; whether 40% is reachable needs to be known where the 6 us goes (softmax vector work versus insufficient K/V reuse)
cheapest_next_discriminator: sweep Bc if the plugin allows it and check whether per-tile time scales roughly linearly (cube-limited) or not (vector-limited)
use the R150 event-probe infrastructure to read cube and vector occupancy inside the FA kernel
